newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Thursday after the market rose early on short-covering following gains by U.S. Treasuries.
"The market was very short," said a trader at a local bank.
Despite the gains, "the market's problems are still there - that is why flows are still very light," he added, pointing to the worries over more hikes in U.S. rates.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.45 to 125.25.
"These days we only have traders' activity with small amounts of little importance," said an analyst.

Even so, some players are beginning to believe the market may have been through its worst patch. They say that from current levels there is more potential for upside than downside, even if the Federal Reserve hikes its Federal funds rate by between 50 and 75 basis points through the year.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.90 percent.
